note: The two double stops that sit inside one minor pentatonic position on the B and high e strings: played in time from the tab, then found on the neck with only their four notes in play, then used to end the learner's own lines. One position on the screen, so no number; the key and tempo move (any key, 60 to 80 bpm), named only as {{=key}}.

exercise.title: Double stops in the {{=key}} minor pentatonic scale
exercise.why: In this position the B and high e strings have two notes at the same fret in two places, so the scale you know already holds two double stops, each played with one finger across both strings.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the backing track, and follow the tab. Each bar goes from one double stop to the other: both notes together, two single notes, then the next double stop.
Practice until the jump from one double stop to the other lands on the beat.

Under this text is the neck with the notes of the {{=key}} minor pentatonic scale, with only the notes of the two double stops in play. Find them on the B and high e strings: {{5}} with {{1}}, and {{b7}} with {{b3}}.

Now every note of the position is in play. Make up short lines from it that end on one of the two double stops.
{{?key}}In another key the position sits on other frets, and the two double stops are still on the B and high e strings, each at one fret.
